text: The correspondence theory of truth holds that a proposition is true if and only if:
choices: it corresponds to a fact — it accurately represents how things stand in a mind-independent reality
it belongs to the maximally coherent and comprehensive system of beliefs
the community of inquirers would converge on it at the ideal limit of inquiry
asserting it is a mere disquotational device that adds nothing to asserting the proposition itself
explanation: Correspondence, defended by the early Russell and the Wittgenstein of the Tractatus, treats truth as a substantive relation between a truth-bearer and a worldly fact. Option 1 is the coherence theory; option 2 is Peirce's pragmatism; option 3 is deflationism, which by contrast denies that truth is any substantive relation at all. The theory's standing burdens are to say what facts are and what the correspondence relation consists in.
